How Does The Economy Influence Voters?
standfirst: The economy is one of the most important factors in how people vote. But its influence has been changing and it has everything to do with politics.

title: As Oil Prices Drop And Money Dries Up, Is The U.S. Shale Boom Going Bust?
standfirst: The boom that helped make the U.S. the world's largest oil producer could be ending. Oil prices are down amid weak demand, and investors no longer seem willing to write the industry a blank check.

title: Niche Products In Our Grocery Stores
standfirst: Niche food products at grocery stores have been getting more and more popular. But, what took so long?

title: Grocery Store Wars
standfirst: The profit margin for groceries is razor thin. To stay competitive against increasingly large competitors like Amazon Prime, retailers are turning to a new service: curbside pickup.

title: Boeing Is So Big That Its 737 Max Production Halt Will Slow The Economy
standfirst: The aircraft giant is the top U.S. exporter, and its decision to suspend production of the 737 Max is likely to ripple through the supply chain. Several analysts project that the move will cut growth.

title: How Online Grocery Delivery Could Help Alleviate Food Deserts
standfirst: Delivery service could make it easier to access fresh, healthy food in these areas, a study finds. It lends support to a pilot program that lets people pay for these groceries with food stamps.

title: U.S.-China Trade Deal Phase 1 Is Here; December Tariffs Are Scrapped
standfirst: China says the deal would cover intellectual property protections and currency manipulation, but no details have been released.

title: Profiles Of America In Full Employment
standfirst: With the jobless rate at a near 50-year low, employers are struggling to fill open positions. An NPR series looks at the consequences and impacts of an economy at full employment.

title: The Work Week, Episode 4: Is The Unemployment Rate Broken?
standfirst: Economist Jared Bernstein thinks it's about time we admit that the unemployment rate is not as useful as it used to be. He offers three alternative indicators.

title: How Hard Are Tariffs Hitting The Economy? It Depends On Who You Ask
standfirst: The U.S. economy is still growing, but trade tensions have taken a toll — especially on factories and farms. The trade war's impact on the overall economy is being debated.

title: Trump Backtracks On Brazil Steel Tariffs
standfirst: President Trump has reversed himself and decided not to impose tariffs on steel and aluminum imported from Brazil. Financial markets were rattled when he abruptly announced a 25% tax on Dec. 2.

title: A Decade Marked By Outrage Over Drug Prices
standfirst: Nearly 1 in 4 Americans has trouble affording prescription drugs, according to a Kaiser Family Foundation poll. Over the past decade, high prices of several medicines have become flashpoints.

title: Job Market Surges As Employers Add 266,000 Jobs In November
standfirst: U.S. employers added a better-than-expected number of jobs last month, boosted in part by the return of General Motors workers who had been on strike in October. The unemployment rate fell to 3.5%.

title: Oil Prices Reflect Concern, Not Panic, After Airstrike On Iranian General
standfirst: Global oil prices rose by about 4% — a modest increase by historical standards — after the U.S. military killed Qassem Soleimani, the leader of Iran's Quds Force, in an airstrike in Baghdad.

title: The Skyrocketing Cost Of Air Ambulances
standfirst: After a catastrophic accident, you may be rushed to the hospital in an air ambulance. It could save your life, but there's no way to predict how much it will cost.

title: Moving Beyond GDP
standfirst: After 75 years, the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis is developing alternative measures of economic well-being.

title: The Cost Of Free: Casper Pays A Price For Generous Mattress Returns
standfirst: Casper changed mattress shopping with the promise of a 100-night "risk-free" trial and easy returns. Now the cost of those returns is being scrutinized as the online company prepares to go public.

title: Patients Still Struggle To Balance High Costs Of MS Treatment, Despite Generic
standfirst: Drugs to treat multiple sclerosis can run $70,000 a year or more. Patients hoped competition from a generic version of one of the most popular brands would spur relief, but prices went up. Here's why.

title: Uber, Lyft, Postmates Refuse To Comply With California Gig Economy Law
standfirst: The new law, which went into effect Wednesday, affects Uber and Lyft drivers as well as journalism freelancers and others. Companies are trying to figure out how to comply or how work around the law.

title: All The Single Ladies...Are Losing In The Housing Market
standfirst: A home is the largest purchase most Americans will ever make. Why single women are losing out in both buying and selling compared to their male counterparts.

title: U.S. Economic Growth Slowed In 2019 To 2.3%
standfirst: The Commerce Department says the U.S. economy grew 2.3% last year. That's slower than the previous year and well below the Trump administration's forecast.

title: The Economic Impact Of An Infectious Disease
standfirst: As the coronavirus spreads internationally, we wanted to know what it looks like when an infectious disease shuts down one of the world's largest economies. We speak with NPR Beijing correspondent, Emily Feng.

title: Jobs Friday: The Racial Unemployment Gap
standfirst: The unemployment rate for black workers is roughly twice that of white workers - and has been for half a century. Today we discuss the reasons for the gap, and how to shrink it.

title: China Will Cut Tariffs In Half On $75 Billion Of U.S. Products
standfirst: The reduced tariffs are to take effect next Feb. 14. The move comes after the Trump administration agreed to halve tariffs on about $112 billion in Chinese goods.

title: 'Gives Me Hope': How Low-Paid Workers Rose Up Against Stagnant Wages
standfirst: When some fast-food workers in New York went on strike one morning in 2012, they had no idea it was the beginning of an unusual movement that would propel an economic revolution.

title: Macy's Closing 125 Stores, Cutting 2,000 Jobs As Mall Stores Struggle
standfirst: The cuts and closures are part of the Macy's attempt to stabilize its finances and rethink its future. It's also trying out smaller stores outside of malls.

title: Listener Questions: Minimum Wage & Gender-Fluid Tadpoles
standfirst: Cardiff takes on the national debt, minimum wage, and gender-fluid tadpoles to get answers to your burning questions.

title: Hiring Picks Up As Employers Add 225,000 Jobs In January
standfirst: U.S. employers added more jobs than expected last month, while the unemployment rate inched up to 3.6%. Unusually warm weather contributed to job gains for construction workers.

title: For Rent: Fast Fashion
standfirst: Buy or rent? That's becoming a question for manufacturers of more and more types of products. Now fast fashion brands are trying to get in on the movement, too.

title: Mortgage Rates Fall To Record Lows. Does It Make Sense To Refinance?
standfirst: Americans are jumping at the chance to save a lot of money by refinancing their home loans — as mortgage rates fall to record lows. Why are rates so low, and when does it pay to refinance?

title: Coronavirus Spreads Recession Fears Around The World
standfirst: U.S. businesses are shutting down plants and watching their sales plummet around the world. Many economists now say odds are increasing that the economy will slow, if not contract altogether.

title: Many Cities Halt Evictions, But Renters Still Need Help
standfirst: In the midst of a pandemic where people are supposed to stay home, many municipalities have halted evictions. But housing advocates want to see more action to help people who can't pay rent.

title: Gas Prices Are Approaching $2
standfirst: Drivers are saving money at the pump, but that's a small silver lining in the big gray cloud of coronavirus-related economic turmoil. AAA says the national average could dive to $2 per gallon soon.

title: United Airlines Threatens To Cut Jobs If Coronavirus Aid Package Isn't Passed
standfirst: Individuals and businesses are slashing air travel. For example, about 624,000 people passed through airport security checkpoints Thursday, compared to 2.4 million people on the same day last year.

title: Are You Affected By Coronavirus-Related Layoffs Or Pay Cuts?
standfirst: Has the coronavirus outbreak affected your employment or income? NPR wants to hear your story.

title: Healthcare And Economic Despair
standfirst: The U.S. spends more on healthcare as a share of its economy than any other wealthy country. In addition to making care less affordable, that also causes indirect damage to the rest of the economy.

title: Average Gas Prices Are Below $2. A Few Stations Are Even Selling For Under $1
standfirst: AAA says the national average is $1.997 per gallon and it's expected to drop further in the coming weeks. In a few places it's less than half that, but most Americans aren't driving much these days.

title: U.S. Economic Slowdown In Coming Months Expected To Be Worst On Record
